title: Тайник Сени и предложение без пирожного  (Senya's Hiding Spot and a Proposal Without Pastry)

segments.t: In the climax of the flashback, while Louis stalls for ten more minutes, Chef Barinov and Nagiyev realize they will have to manage the evening without any pastries at all. Back in the present, Barinov reflects on how Senya's habit of stealing food nearly derailed the owner's engagement.
И потом у него есть тайное место.
Давайте в ваше кольцо я спрячу его пирожное.

'Well, what is going on in here?' In Russian, the idea of 'come on' flows naturally into 'is going on' without extra filler words.
'Where is the dessert?' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'dessert' before landing on 'where'.
'Louis, where is the dessert?' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'Louis' and finishing on 'dessert'. Max answers right away.
'We just need to wait a little bit longer.' Notice how Russian expresses 'needs to be' and 'to wait' with crisp inflection rather than helper words.
'Where is the ring?' Louis anchors the line on 'ring', while 'where' completes the thought.
'Vitya, what on earth is that?' Max raises the pitch on 'such a' to turn the phrase into a direct spoken question. Louis answers right away.
'It is much safer this way.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'like this' before landing on 'safe'.
'Look how big that guy is.' The grammar packs 'look' and 'healthy' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
И потом у него есть тайное место.
'And besides, he has a secret hiding spot.' Notice how Russian expresses 'both' and 'station' with crisp inflection rather than helper words. Max answers right away.

'Let me hide your ring inside a pastry for him.' In Russian, the idea of 'let's' flows naturally into 'pastries' without extra filler words.
'It will take about ten minutes.' The meaning hinges on 'this' working together with 'ten' in spoken Russian.
'Right now, coming right up.' Notice how Russian expresses 'any minute' and 'any minute' with crisp inflection rather than helper words. Louis answers right away.
'We will manage without pastries from now on.' The meaning hinges on 'without' working together with 'now' in spoken Russian. Now let's listen to the entire scene again without interruption.
